answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity costly: every new agent must lock collateral in a bond that is slashed if it votes twice or impersonates peers. Reputation accrues only to bonded agents, so a voyage of fake accounts needs N times the stake for N votes while the payoff stays fixed. Like a comet that cannot hide its tail, duplicated behavior leaves traceable links between accounts. At the zenith of this design, an attacker forfeits more in bonds than any single vote can return, turning sybil attacks into a losing trade.
